symptom: `log info node 'Mod' 'Item {number} not found';` and a REST POST's `Body: template '{}'` printed "Check passed!"; mx check then reported [CE0712] "Brace should be followed by a number of digits or another brace." at the Log message / Call REST service activity (ako/mxcli#1397, mendixlabs/mxcli#1515; reported on 11.12.5 and 11.15). Four of mxcli's own docs taught the failing JSON body `template '{"name": "{1}"}'`, and MDL-WF21 / MDL-WIDGET04 refused the legal `{{1}}` as an unfilled {1}.
cause: Nothing modelled the template grammar: the only template checks counted placeholders with a `\{(\d+)\}` regexp (CE0720 for workflow texts and dynamic text/button captions), which never sees a malformed brace and counts the escaped `{{1}}` as a placeholder. Microflow templates (log, show message, validation feedback, send email, REST URL/body, Java action text template) had no placeholder check at all.
file: `mdl/texttemplate/texttemplate.go` (Check, Placeholders — the grammar), `mdl/executor/template_text_grammar.go` (templateTextRefusal = the one decision, MDL-TEMPLATE02, checkTemplateGrammar / refuseTemplateGrammar), wired in validate_microflow/nanoflow/alter_flow/program, the four builders in cmd_microflows_builder_calls.go and javaActionTemplateValue; `validate_workflow_templates.go` and `validate_widgets.go` use the same scanner; tests `mdl/texttemplate/texttemplate_test.go`, `mdl/executor/template_text_grammar_test.go`; fixtures `mdl-examples/bug-tests/template-braces-1397-brace-grammar{,.fail}.mdl`
insight: Measure the slot x input matrix in ONE project with `mx check -j` (one document per text, the JSON names the document): 60 inputs x up to 12 slots took one mxbuild run per version, and 10.24.24, 11.13.0 and 11.15.0 agreed on every cell they shared (478 between 11.13 and 11.15, 540 between 10.24 and 11.15), which is what licenses one shared grammar instead of per-slot rules. The full CE family is in Mendix.Modeler.Texts.dll (`strings -el | grep -i brace`): CE0712 non-digit after `{`, CE0713 digits then end, CE0714 digits then not `}`, CE0716 `{0}`, CE0717 past int32 (also a non-ASCII digit, which IsDigit accepts and Parse refuses), CE0720 index > params — one per text, first in reading order, CE0720 only for an otherwise clean text. The surprising accepts are the controls that decide the predicate: a lone `}`, `}}`, a `{` that ENDS the text, `{01}` and `{{1}}` all build, so a regexp in either direction over-fires. A matrix parser keyed on letters-only case names silently dropped every case with a digit in its name and made `{2147483646}` look accepted — check the harness against a row you know before trusting a surprising cell. Pluggable widget textTemplates are not covered: mxcli rewrites their named `{Attr}` placeholders to `{1}` first. Side find: mxcli-written workflows do not load on 10.24.24 (TypeCacheUnknownTypeException Workflows$StartWorkflowActivity).
